source: I have a sense that time is somehow repeating itself, and I've lived through this before.
Ophelia... are you all right?
Yes. It's not my health, it's... something else.
Are you certain? The last time you were ill...
I know. I covered it up. But I was a child then. It won't happen again.
I'm not as fragile as I used to be, Bernardo. You don't always have to look out for me.
I wouldn't watch you so closely if you didn't make me worry so often.
I don't know why, but I've lived through this same day once before, as if time is repeating.
Have a lie down for a bit. That usually does the trick when I feel that way.
So... you feel this way, too?
Of course. A nice wine, an excellent book... so many things can make you feel so differently about the world!
Not what I meant.
Sure, 'Feely. Loony as a bat, huh?
Whatever you say! Just don't stab me to death in a fit of insane rage, or something.
How about this: I back away slowly, and you stop talking about time-repeating nonsense. Yes? Yes.
Thanks, Brit.
It is a familiar tale.
It's said Queen Astrid was overcome with similar illness once. But that was very long ago.
Queen... Astrid?
And there I've said too much.
Time is repeating itself, and I feel... lost.
Is this a new game?
I'm sorry, Ophelia, but I haven't the time to play it.
I'm a very busy man. And besides, I don't like games of any sort.
Your wife was having an affair with Claudius before your death. Did you know?
Yes. As we've discussed before, it has never been a concern of mine.
Yes. I knew.
It doesn't seem to trouble you.
It does not.
I made my peace with it long before my death.
Though they were only one in body near the end of my life... their feelings for one another extended to far before that.
Something in Gerta and I died far sooner, when the others did.
The others?
Ah. It would not be common knowledge for anyone other than Irma and Gerta, I expect.
Hamlet was our first living child. But Gerta was with child before that. Four times in all.
The first she lost very near to birth. We thought the child might live, but we were wrong.
The second and third emerged simply as a stream of blood.
She saw each loss as a failure unto herself.
After we lost our third child, I no longer knew what to say to her, and she to me.
If she could not give me an heir, she could not fulfill her duties as Queen, as she saw them. And to her, that was the gravest failing of all.
When she was with child a fourth time, she had already picked out a place to bury him in the graveyard, so certain was she that he would die.
But Hamlet lived. And our miracle son was born.
Claudius knew nothing of the lost children, as far as I know. He was a comfort to her. He was warm and gentle to her in ways I was not.
Over time that comfort grew to familiarity, then to affection, then to love. I witnessed it and I did not stop it.
My wife has suffered enough in this life. Improper though it may be for a man to allow his wife to be wooed by his brother...
If it would purchase her one single shred of happiness, I would overlook nearly anything in the world for Gerta.
I-- I had no idea. My sincerest apologies for prying, King Hamlet.
The Queen was having an affair with Claudius before her husband passed away. Did you know?
Gertrude? I-- I don't know quite what to say about that.
Though I suppose it doesn't entirely surprise me.
If I recall correctly, the Queen came to Elsinore when she was quite young.
She was raised with both Hamlet senior and Claudius as two of her closest companions.
She was always betrothed to Hamlet, I heard, but perhaps there was something in her friendship with Claudius as well.
Regardless, that's the sort of unsavory thing I prefer not to discuss in depth.
It wouldn't be beyond Hamlet to lie about a thing like that. I don't know that I believe what I heard, myself.
Oh, my.
I didn't. But what a devastating thing that might be.
Don't tell Guilda about it, or she'll never stop asking me what I think His Highness looks like in the nude.
Are you quite serious? Everyone knows, now.
As I predicted, Guilda won't stop asking me what I think His Highness looks like in the nude.
Umm, no, but now I'm imagining them both naked.
So thanks for that.
I assumed you're the one who tipped off Hamlet. And we all saw how that turned out!
The Queen was having an affair with Claudius before King Hamlet's death.
Stale gossip is also the most tedious, 'Feely. Everyone knows that now.
And how could you possibly know that, exactly?
I have my ways.
Don't use that phrase. It makes you sound like a creep.
Anyway, I already knew, of course. Rifling through the Queen's personal belongings has been my only means of entertainment recently.
But now that others are blathering on about it... well, I guess there's no reason to keep this a secret, is there?
I need access to the Queen's personal chambers. Can you help me?
Have you some need to pay respects to her?
Either way, it matters little. I was ordered to hand over my key after her passing. And so I have.
I have a key. What need do you have of it?
I'd just like to take a quick look around. There's something I'm looking for.
Rummaging around in my lady's chambers? Hah! Guts, but no tact!
Everyone knows you're too curious for your own good, my lady.
Isn't there something I could do for you in return? A favor of sorts?
Mmm. A woman who strikes deals. Far too few of those around. Ja, I'll bite.
I've been known to gamble now and then. But the cowards who play with me are too delicate to play my favorite trick-taker: Ruff and Honours.
Instead, they stick to only the games they think they can win!
Round up my card partners, persuade them, and you'll have yourself an exchange.
(Not to mention, if the Guard Captain sees me rousing up his men for 'immoral' behavior... he'll be furious. The pious lout.)
That'd be Horatio, Marcellus, and the good Lady Brit, of course.
That'd be Horatio and Marcellus, of course. Ordinarily, it'd be Brit too, but...
Rather a shame to hear the news.
If you tell them all I want to strike up a game, come back here. Only then I shall unlock the room for you!
Certainly. You're in luck -- Bernardo ordered me to turn over the key, but he hasn't come for it yet.
Gertrude was never my favorite noblewoman to wait upon, but for what it's worth, she was kind to me.
So all I ask is, whatever you find in there, be kind to her memory. Understand?
And you'll need to do me a favor, of course.
What do you need?
Certainly, I have a key to her rooms.
But I smell the beginnings of a good deal. Nothing comes free in this world, 'Feely.
I want to speak to the Prince privately, but he won't even give me a second glance.
If you arrange a rendezvous, on the other hand... maybe he'll show.
Tell him I want to meet him in the garden tonight and then I'll unlock that room for you.
Oh, and definitely don't tell anyone else. I want privacy.
Oh, and definitely don't tell anyone else. I want the utmost privacy, and you know how Gertrude can be.
Not to mention I don't want you pining for him off in the corner somewhere.
Everyone knows how that ended.
So keep it discreet, won't you?
... Fine. But don't say I haven't ever done anything nice for you.
Less talking, more working. Go.
My lord, I'd like to seek permission to enter the Queen's personal chambers.
You what?
My wife is dead, and you come to me seeking to rifle through her room?
Vultures. All of you. Disgusting little vultures.
None of you ever understood us.
No. Absolutely not.
My apologies. It's just--
I don't think I can go back there again so soon.
Perhaps soon I could find the strength to enter that place. But not now. I'll think on it.
Ho ho... I haven't had access to my wife's rooms in months. Sorry, I don't have a key.
I appreciate that she's in mourning and needs her privacy. Only Irma and Brit are allowed to enter.
My lady, I'd like to seek permission to enter your personal chambers.
Ophelia, if you'd like to chat, I'm perfectly happy to meet you in the garden. Or the gallery.
Might I just have a... quick peek at your rooms, then?
No, Ophelia. This is strange of you. And unusually uncouth.
I tried to get into your mother's chambers, but they were locked.
Oh, that. Never mind that now. I've little care for what has come before.
It's time to focus on what lies before us.
Of course they're locked! Why do you think I haven't looked around myself?
Brit and Irma have keys. Not even my uncle is permitted to enter.
Why would you want to go in there?
A den of sin and incestuous heat. That's all it is, in the end.
(Right. He didn't ask me to search her room in this timeline.)
(I bet he'd still be interested in whatever I learn, though...)
There's nothing in there I want to know about anymore. Not now.
Even if that weren't wildly inappropriate, love, I haven't got a key.
Her nosy little lady-in-waiting and that Bohemian bullish cook are the only people she ever trusted with that honor.
But I stand resolute: you musn't go into her rooms, Ophelia.
I'm... not sure if I should, Ophelia. She locks her doors for a reason.
Besides, I don't have a key. Only Lady Brit, Irma, and the Queen do. I'd need to request it from one of them.
Absolutely not. In fact, I've requested all available keys from both Lady Brit and Irma.
We're still uncovering details about the circumstances involved in her death. Please don't get underfoot.
I donno if I should, Ophelia. Queen likes 'er privacy. It's ladies-only, as far as I know.
Only Brit, Irma, and Her Highness 'ave keys to get in.
I donno if I should, Ophelia. Bernardo asked for all of the keys back after she passed.
Feels wrong to be preyin' on the dead.
Only Brit, Irma, and Her Highness ever 'ad keys to get in, anyway.
Irma wants to play a specific card game with you. Ruff and Honors.
Ugh. The last time I played that one with that witch, she destroyed me so badly I was out of drinking coin for three months.
So... is that a 'no'?
Are you kidding? Of course I'll play.
Now it's my turn to bring her to her knees.
